resource: CS50P (CS50's Introduction to Programming with Python)
cost_account: Free to read/watch, no account. Free CS50 ID/GitHub account only if using check50/style50 autograder or submitting for a certificate.
rights_detail: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, confirmed on-page at cs50.harvard.edu/python/license/
summary_judgment: SELECTED STARTING SOURCE. Highest strong-coverage count (seven C-ids at 3) of any single general Python resource evaluated; only candidate with a dedicated Unit Tests week (C10) and a dedicated OOP week (C08); autograded practice loop is the strongest of the group. Does not cover Git/GitHub (C12) or AI-aware programming (C13) -- filled separately.

cost_account: Free, no account, always available offline as downloadable docs bundle too.
rights_detail: PSF License v2 for docs; code examples dual-licensed PSF/0BSD since Python 3.8.6
summary_judgment: Best-in-class REFERENCE backbone (authoritative, most permissive license, most durable link granularity) but the tutorial itself states it assumes some programming background, and it has no built-in practice/feedback loop. Kept as the canonical reference layer under CS50P, not the primary teaching spine.

resource: Python for Everybody (PY4E), book + Runestone interactive edition
cost_account: Free, no account for the static book; optional free account on the interactive Runestone edition to save progress.
rights_detail: CC BY 4.0 per py4e.com/materials and the py4e GitHub repo
summary_judgment: Renowned true-novice clarity and the most permissive license found (CC BY 4.0, no NC/SA constraint), but weak on C08 (OOP is minimal by design) and C10 (little formal testing/debugging instruction). Strong second-layer or Week-2/Week-10-11 supplemental candidate.

resource: Runestone Academy -- Foundations of Python Programming (FOPP)
cost_account: Free to read, no account required to read; optional free account to save progress/track completion.
rights_detail: GNU Free Documentation License 1.3+; Runestone platform code is MIT
summary_judgment: Strongest embedded practice/feedback of the pure-text candidates (Parsons problems, auto-graded exercises inline) and the most permissively licensed textbook (GFDL, explicitly redistributable/modifiable). A very close second to CS50P; would be the pick if built-in unit-testing instruction (C10) mattered less relative to interactivity.

resource: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 2e (Al Sweigart)
cost_account: Free to read online, no account.
summary_judgment: Not selected as backbone (uneven depth, weak OOP, no autograding), but its CSV/JSON/file-handling chapters are the most practically thorough of anything reviewed. Recommended narrowly as the C09 hole-filling supplement.

resource: Software Carpentry -- Plotting and Programming in Python
rights_detail: CC BY 4.0 lessons; MIT example code
summary_judgment: Data/plotting framing is a workshop-for-researchers genre, weaker fit for Coding Odyssey worlds and missing OOP/testing entirely. Not recommended (see Section G).

cost_account: Free, requires account for mentoring/progress tracking.
rights_detail: Exercism repos are split per-language; at least one track (bash) confirmed MIT, but the Python track's own repo license was not individually re-verified in this pass -- treat as unclear until confirmed.
summary_judgment: Best pure practice/mentoring-feedback loop reviewed, and a real candidate for reinforcing C10 (testing/debugging) since every exercise ships with a test suite. Held at metadata-only pending an explicit per-repo license check before any exercise text is copied.

cost_account: Free, requires a free GitHub account to run the interactive exercise.
summary_judgment: HOLE-FILLER (C12). Official, free, hands-on (real repo/PR practice with automated progress checks). Selected filler for the Git/GitHub hole.

resource: GitHub Docs -- Review AI-generated code (Copilot tutorial)
rights_detail: CC BY 4.0, confirmed via github/docs repository LICENSE file
summary_judgment: HOLE-FILLER (C13). Reputable, current, primary-source guidance on reviewing/testing AI-generated code; written for working developers rather than CS1 novices, so it is a supplement the instructor should frame, not a self-contained lesson. Best available free option found; flagged in Section E as a partial fill, not a full one.
